To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PIVC receives inputs from the vestibular and proprioceptive systems as well as from visual cortex, and that the PIVCs response is a function of the motion of the body, the motion of visual objects, and the motion of the eyes, but is not correlated with the motion or orientation of the head.
the parietoinsular vestibular cortex contains multisensory neurons with a continuous spectrum of visual, vestibulo-proprioceptive and vestibular responses.

the PIVC contains a population of multisensory neurons that are responsive to the motion of the body and the visual world, and that this information is used to compare the motion of the self with that of the external world.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vestibular information in the cerebral cortex.
how the nervous system processes sensory information to generate adaptive behavior.
the neural basis of the perception of motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the parietoinsular cortex is involved in multisensory convergence for self-motion, body, and head movement and external visual object motion, and is involved in the comparison of the movement of these objects in space and in relation to each other.

the PIVC represents the motion of the self and external objects in a common reference frame, and that it does not represent the motion of the eyes, head, body, or visual target relative to one another.
the PIVC is a multisensory convergence zone for the processing of self and visual motion in space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PIVC represents the movement of the head, body, eyes, and visual objects in space, and that this information is used to compare and coordinate the movements of the body with those of external visual objects.
the PIVC is an area of the brain with multisensory convergence that compares self and external motion.
the PIVC is a cortical area that integrates vestibular, proprioceptive and visual signals to represent the motion of the body, head and visual targets relative to the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PIVC is not a single structure, but a complex network of multisensory neurons with a wide range of functional properties.
the PIVC does not represent a specific sensory modality.
there is a continuum of responses in the PIVCs, with some cells being more strongly tuned to a specific modality and others responding equivalently to multiple modalities.
